title: FP&A Revenue Forecast with Back-testing — real marketplace data (Olist)
upload_text:
TITLE
FP&A Revenue Forecast with Back-testing — real marketplace data (Olist)

SHORT DESCRIPTION
Real data, not demo: monthly revenue of Olist, a Brazilian marketplace (public dataset, MIT licence). Instead of drawing a trend line, I back-tested three transparent methods on Mar–Aug 2018, picked the one with the lowest error, added Black Friday and December factors from 2017, and gave Sep–Dec 2018 as a range. Finding: the 2017 trend line badly over-forecasts 2018 as growth flattened; the latest run-rate wins (9% error vs 25%). Fully formula-driven in Excel with an assumptions table finance can change.

SKILLS / TAGS
FP&A, Forecasting, Financial Planning, Excel Modelling, Back-testing, Business Analysis

title: Three-way Data Reconciliation — orders vs items vs payments (real Olist data)
upload_text:
TITLE
Three-way Data Reconciliation — orders vs items vs payments (real Olist data)

SHORT DESCRIPTION
Real data, not demo: all 99,441 orders from Olist, a Brazilian marketplace (public dataset, MIT licence). I rebuilt each order's value from its items and freight, matched it to payment lines, and classified every order into six reconciliation statuses with an exceptions list. Result: 99.6% match to the cent; 775 orders (about R$163k) were paid but never shipped and need confirmed refunds; 94% of over-payments are instalment interest. Delivered as a repeatable monthly control in Excel.

SKILLS / TAGS
Data Reconciliation, Data Quality, Finance Operations, Excel, Controls, Audit Support

title: Operations Efficiency — seller fulfilment performance (real Olist data)
upload_text:
TITLE
Operations Efficiency — seller fulfilment performance (real Olist data)

SHORT DESCRIPTION
Real data, not demo: 788 sellers with 20+ orders on Olist, a Brazilian marketplace (public dataset, MIT licence), covering 88% of delivered orders. I measured each seller's hand-over time and shipping cut-off misses and linked them to late deliveries and reviews. Findings: the worst 10% of sellers cause a third of cut-off misses; sellers missing 20%+ of cut-offs have twice the late rate; Friday–Saturday approvals wait over a day longer; seller size makes no difference. Formula-driven Excel with a performance-management plan.

SKILLS / TAGS
Operations Analytics, Process Improvement, SLA Management, Vendor Performance, Excel, Dashboard

title: PMO Portfolio Analytics — budget growth and schedule slippage (real Government of Canada IT projects)
upload_text:
TITLE
PMO Portfolio Analytics — budget growth and schedule slippage (real Government of Canada IT projects)

SHORT DESCRIPTION
Real data, not demo: 1,126 Government of Canada IT projects over C$1M reported to Parliament in 2016, 2019 and 2022. I tracked the 192 projects reported more than once and compared their first and latest budgets and end dates. Findings: budgets grew 37% (C$4.0B to C$5.5B); 86% finish later than first promised (median 2 years); projects that slipped 2+ years grew their budget about 75%; the top 10 overruns are over half of all added cost. Formula-driven Excel with a PMO dashboard and governance recommendations.

SKILLS / TAGS
PMO, Project Portfolio Management, Project Controls, Excel Dashboard, Governance, Data Analysis

title: CRM & Sales Ops — from lead to first sale (real Olist funnel data)
upload_text:
TITLE
CRM & Sales Ops — from lead to first sale (real Olist funnel data)

SHORT DESCRIPTION
Real data, not demo: Olist's seller-acquisition funnel (public dataset) — about 6,000 marketing-qualified leads and 842 closed deals, joined to real marketplace sales. I measured conversion by channel and, more importantly, whether signed sellers ever started selling. Findings: 13% of leads close; search converts about 15% vs 4–6% for email and social; about half of won sellers never made a sale; activation and revenue differ strongly by lead type and sales rep. Formula-driven Excel with a rep scorecard and onboarding recommendations.

CRM Analytics, Sales Operations, Funnel Analysis, Sales Rep Scorecard, Excel Dashboard, Lead Management

title: Process Improvement — IT incident handling: where the time goes (real Volvo IT event log)
upload_text:
TITLE
Process Improvement — IT incident handling: where the time goes (real Volvo IT event log)

SHORT DESCRIPTION
Real data, not demo: 7,554 IT incidents and 65,000+ status changes from Volvo IT's incident-management process (public BPI Challenge 2013 event log). I rebuilt each incident's path from the raw log and measured hand-offs between support groups, "ping-pong" bounces and time in each status. Findings: incidents with no hand-off average 5 days open vs 44 with five or more hand-offs; bounced incidents stay open about 3x longer; about 70% of the time before resolution is spent waiting or queued. Delivered as an Excel analysis with dashboard and concrete process changes.

SKILLS / TAGS
Process Improvement, Process Mining, Lean, IT Service Management, Root Cause Analysis, Excel Dashboard

title: M&E Results Framework — tracking a global programme against its targets (real WHO / Our World in Data)
upload_text:
TITLE
M&E Results Framework — tracking a global programme against its targets (real WHO / Our World in Data)

SHORT DESCRIPTION
Real data, not demo: COVID-19 vaccination coverage for 203 countries (Our World in Data, CC BY) tracked against the WHO global milestones of 10%, 40% and 70% fully vaccinated. I built a results framework with achievement rates, disaggregation by income group and continent, trend lines and a traffic-light gap rating. Findings: 56% of countries met 40% by end-2021 and only 30% met 70% by mid-2022; no low-income country met either on time; the 60% world average hid 13% in low-income countries. Formula-driven Excel M&E dashboard.

SKILLS / TAGS
Monitoring & Evaluation, Results Framework, Indicator Tracking, Development Data, Excel Dashboard, Reporting

title: Retail Sales Analysis — products, orders and markets (real UK online retailer data)
upload_text:
TITLE
Retail Sales Analysis — products, orders and markets (real UK online retailer data)

SHORT DESCRIPTION
Real data, not demo: 541,909 raw transaction lines from a UK online gift retailer (UCI Online Retail dataset, CC BY 4.0). I cleaned duplicates, postage/fee lines, stock adjustments and cancellations (including orders reversed in full), then built product and order tables and analysed seasonality, product concentration (Pareto), order size, export markets and weekday pattern. Findings: revenue peaks in November at about 2.5 times January; the top 20% of products bring 78% of revenue; orders of £1,000+ are under 9% of orders but about 45% of sales. Formula-driven Excel with dashboard and actions.

SKILLS / TAGS
Retail Analytics, Sales Analysis, Pareto / ABC Analysis, Data Cleaning, Excel Dashboard, Seasonality

title: Marketing Campaign Analysis — who to call, how often, and on which channel (real bank campaign data)
upload_text:
TITLE
Marketing Campaign Analysis — who to call, how often, and on which channel (real bank campaign data)

SHORT DESCRIPTION
Real data, not demo: 41,188 clients contacted in a Portuguese bank's term-deposit phone campaigns, 2008–2010 (UCI Bank Marketing, CC BY 4.0). I measured conversion, calls per sale and lift by previous outcome, channel, occupation, age and number of calls, and modelled a 3-call cap. Findings: past "yes" clients convert at about 65% vs 11% overall; conversion drops from 13% on the first call to 3% after 11+; mobile beats landline almost 3x; a 3-call cap saves about a quarter of calls. Formula-driven Excel with a targeting plan.

Marketing Analytics, Campaign Analysis, Customer Segmentation, Telemarketing, Excel Dashboard, Targeting

title: Customer Churn & Retention — who stops buying, and who is about to (real online retail data)
upload_text:
TITLE
Customer Churn & Retention — who stops buying, and who is about to (real online retail data)

SHORT DESCRIPTION
Real data, not demo: 4,300+ registered customers of a UK online retailer (UCI Online Retail, CC BY 4.0). I built a customer table (orders, spend, recency, usual buying gap), measured 90-day lapse by order count and spend, built a monthly cohort retention matrix and an early-warning list of regulars who are late for their next order. Findings: 43% of customers lapsed but they are only about 11% of revenue; lapse falls from 49% at two orders to 2% at 10+; about 1 in 5 new customers buys again the next month; 92 overdue regulars (about £310k lifetime spend) to contact now.

SKILLS / TAGS
Churn Analysis, Customer Retention, Cohort Analysis, CRM Analytics, Excel Dashboard, Customer Segmentation

title: Manufacturing Productivity — garment lines vs daily targets (real factory data)
upload_text:
TITLE
Manufacturing Productivity — garment lines vs daily targets (real factory data)

SHORT DESCRIPTION
Real data, not demo: 1,197 team-days from the sewing and finishing lines of a garment factory, Jan–Mar 2015 (UCI dataset, CC BY 4.0). I cleaned the data and measured how often each department and team met its daily productivity target, with weekly trend, idle-time and style-change analysis. Findings: target met on 73% of team-days — sewing about 83%, finishing about 60%. finishing teams 6–8 meet target on only about a third of days; on idle-time days sewing met target only 1 day in 5. Formula-driven Excel with dashboard and improvement plan.

Manufacturing Analytics, Productivity Analysis, Operations, Lean, Excel Dashboard, KPI Tracking

title: HR Analytics — workforce mix and gender pay benchmark (real US Census data)
upload_text:
TITLE
HR Analytics — workforce mix and gender pay benchmark (real US Census data)

SHORT DESCRIPTION
Real data, not demo: US Census median earnings of full-time workers for 522 occupations, 2013–2016, plus BLS history since 1979. I built worker-weighted pay ratios by occupation group, by how female-dominated a job is, and over time, and listed the widest gaps among large occupations. Findings: within the same occupations women earned about 83% of men's median pay in 2016, almost unchanged since 2013; financial managers are among the widest gaps (about 62%); female-dominated jobs pay much less on average. Built as a benchmark an HR team can compare its own pay data against.

SKILLS / TAGS
HR Analytics, Pay Equity, Compensation Benchmarking, Workforce Analytics, Excel Dashboard, People Analytics
